data.one_liner: Add customizable page transitions like slide, fade, scale, and rotate for Navigator and go_router.
data.what_it_does: Provides 18 ready-made transition animations (such as slide, fade, scale, rotation, size, and diagonal effects) that can be applied to imperative Navigator pushes, named routes, or declarative routers like go_router. It supports full control over duration, reverse duration, curves, and reverse curves without boilerplate PageRouteBuilder code.
use_when: You want custom entry and exit animations for screen transitions without writing boilerplate PageRouteBuilders.
You are using go_router or another Navigator 2.0 router and need custom page transition routes.
You want to standardize page transitions across imperative and declarative navigation.
avoid_when: You are handling complex hero animations or shared element transitions between pages.
You prefer default platform-specific native page transitions.
strengths: Includes 18 built-in transition types covering slides, fades, scales, rotations, and diagonals.
Works seamlessly with both imperative Navigator navigation and declarative routers like go_router.
Allows fine-grained customization of duration, reverse duration, and easing curves.
weaknesses: Limited to standard page transition animations rather than custom multi-widget hero morphs.
Does not replace a routing library on its own; it only handles the transition animations.

alternatives.name: auto_route
alternatives.why_pick_it: Pick auto_route if you want full declarative routing with code generation and built-in transition support rather than manual widget wrappers.

alternatives.name: go_router
alternatives.why_pick_it: Pick go_router if you are adopting official declarative routing, though this package can be used alongside it for custom transitions.
